title: Greedy Algorithms
subtitle: Step through locally optimal choices, track feasibility constraints, and see where the greedy-choice property holds — or breaks.

activity-selection.name: Activity Selection
activity-selection.shortDesc: Sort intervals by earliest finish time and accept every non-overlapping activity.
activity-selection.complexityNote: Sorting by earliest finish time dominates · Greedy exchange argument proves optimality

fractional-knapsack.name: Fractional Knapsack
fractional-knapsack.shortDesc: Order items by value/weight density and pack whole or fractional portions until full.
fractional-knapsack.complexityNote: Orders items by value-to-weight density descending · Optimal because items are divisible

greedy-coin-change.name: Greedy Coin Change
greedy-coin-change.shortDesc: Repeatedly pick the largest fitting coin and compare against the DP global optimum.
greedy-coin-change.complexityNote: Optimal on canonical coin systems (e.g. US coins) · Can fail on non-canonical sets like [1, 3, 4]

controls.activitiesHint: Comma-separated, up to 12 intervals with start < end
controls.itemsHint: Comma-separated, up to 10 items with positive weights

coin.title: Denomination selection & remainder
coin.verdictOptimalBody: For these denominations and target, taking the largest fitting coin achieves the exact minimum coin count.
coin.verdictSuboptimalBody: The largest-first choice committed to coin {{first}} too early, using {{greedyCount}} coins instead of the optimal {{optCount}}.
coin.verdictFailedBody: Greedy left remainder {{remaining}}, even though an exact {{optCount}}-coin DP solution exists.
coin.verdictImpossibleBody: Neither greedy nor dynamic programming can form this exact target with the given denominations.
